title: Every template encodes a finitely branching omega-tree, uniquely up to local isomorphism, with branches controlled by branches of the template

core_obligations: Clause (i): build the finitely branching tree level by level, keeping a bijection between the n-th level P_n of the template and a partition pi_n of the n-th level L_n of the tree, and adjoining n_i new points above each x in X for the members Y_i of P_{n+1} above X (proof lines 597-608).

Clause (ii): observe that the construction leaves the new points unordered, so two trees built from the same template behave identically up to every finite level even if they are not isomorphic, which is exactly local isomorphism (proof lines 610-614).
Clause (iii): translate an eventually singleton omega-branch of the template into the corresponding balanced subtree of the tree, which is then eventually a single branch (proof lines 616-617).

Clause (iv): index a Fraenkel-Mostowski model by the members of the tree, let the group be induced by the tree automorphisms fixing each member of the template, and use that each subtree coming from an omega-branch of the template is balanced with infinitely many non-singleton entries, hence has no infinite branch in the model; since every infinite branch would arise that way, there is none (proof lines 619-625).
proof_roadmap: Construct the tree from the template level by level and record the partition bookkeeping that keeps the two in step (proof lines 597-608).
Read local isomorphism off the freedom of the construction, translate branches of the template into subtrees, and run the finite-support model argument for the negative clause (proof lines 610-625).
difficulty_reason: The lemma relates a template (T*, prec) to finitely branching omega-trees encoded by it: it produces one such tree, shows any two are locally isomorphic, links eventually singleton branches of the template to infinite branches of the tree, and proves that in a suitable finite-support model a template with no eventually singleton branch can encode a tree with no infinite branch at all (statement lines 588-595). The proof constructs the tree level by level while maintaining a bijection between the levels of the template and partitions of the levels of the tree (proof lines 597-608), then argues that the construction's freedom to leave the new points unordered is exactly what produces locally isomorphic but possibly non-isomorphic trees (proof lines 610-614), and finally runs a Fraenkel-Mostowski argument in which the group fixes the template and every would-be infinite branch lives inside a balanced subtree with infinitely many non-singleton entries (proof lines 619-625). The clause that carries the content is the last one, since it is the only place where the absence of choice is used; the first three clauses are a construction and two observations about it. H2.
